samples.summary: New dispose-revokes-mutators / `isDisposed()` write-boundary rule is not recorded in `docs/design/sharing.md`
samples.evidence: sharing.md §"Docs Package (Read-Only Mode)" (lines 163-192) and §Security (lines 200-219) enumerate exactly how the client-side write boundary is built — `initialize(container, store, theme, readOnly)`, the `EditorAPI` mutating-method allowlist, the neutered `DocStore` from `store/read-only.ts` (#989), and why the flag is load-bearing while the auth webhook is in shadow mode. This delta adds a second, orthogonal revocation mechanism to that same boundary: `dispose()` now calls `neuterMutations(api)` unconditionally (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts, dispose), a new `EditorAPI.isDisposed()` contract that async callers MUST consult after any `await` (editor.ts EditorAPI doc comment), and frontend callers acting on it (image-insert.ts:145, :195). None of that appears in the canonical subsystem doc, so the doc now describes only half of the boundary it claims to describe.
searchedFor: glob docs/design/**/*.md for a docs read-only doc

samples.summary: `docs-collaboration.md` §"The undo floor is an entry, not a depth" now contradicts the implementation, which is entry *and* depth
samples.evidence: The design doc (lines 400-412) states the floor is held by the identity of the top entry and that "an entry that has itself been dropped is simply not found, which is exactly the ... answer a depth cannot give". After this delta `YorkieDocStore` keeps three pieces of state (`undoFloorMark`, `undoFloorDepth`, `undoFloorIdentityUsable`), probes identity-stability at mark time, refreshes a depth on every successful lookup, falls back to the depth comparison when identity is unusable, and latches the floor away only when `stack.length >= YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH` (yorkie-doc-store.ts canUndo). The documented shape is no longer the implemented shape; the doc heading is now actively misleading for the next reader of `canUndo()`.

samples.summary: Undo-floor hardening is scope creep for this PR and re-hardcodes an unexported SDK constant, deepening the documented Docs/Slides divergence
samples.evidence: This delta's stated purpose is the dispose/`isDisposed()` revocation path; the `YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH = 50` constant, the identity-stability probe, and the cap-based latch defend against a hypothetical future change in `getUndoStackForTest()` semantics rather than any observed defect. The literal 50 duplicates the SDK's unexported `MaxUndoRedoStackDepth` (also restated in packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3808 and docs-collaboration.md:328), so the same unowned number now lives in three places. Meanwhile `docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:180` says the Slides store must "Mirror Docs ... including the undo floor", and `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:347` is still the plain depth counter — the two stores now answer "can I undo?" by materially different rules while a design doc asserts they mirror each other.

samples.summary: Disposal revokes only the `EditorAPI` methods, not the live `getStore()` / `getDoc()` handles — the same gap #989 closed for `readOnly` has no counterpart here
samples.evidence: `dispose()` sets `disposed` and calls `neuterMutations(api)`, and the `EditorAPI.isDisposed` doc comment claims "A disposed editor is inert — every mutating method has been neutered". The read-only branch's own comment (editor.ts, `if (readOnly)`) explains that a name allowlist cannot guard handles it merely returns, and that `getStore()`/`getDoc()` are covered instead by `readOnlyDocStore` (#989). Under disposal there is no such coverage: a stale holder that captured the API before an `editor`→`viewer` downgrade can still call `api.getStore().insertText(...)` or write through `api.getDoc()` on a non-readOnly-built editor, which is exactly the escape route this delta claims disposal closes. Existing callers do reach the document that way (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:66-67 drives find/replace through `getDoc()`/`getStore()`), so the boundary the change asserts is not the boundary it implements.
searchedFor: read editor.ts readOnly branch and dispose()

samples.summary: `isDisposed()` puts the burden on every async caller to opt in, with nothing enforcing it
samples.evidence: The new contract ("Ask this after any `await` before reporting success to the user") is honoured at exactly two call sites (image-insert.ts:145 and :195). Nothing in the API makes a post-disposal write detectable by default — the neutered methods return `void`/`Promise<void>` and silently succeed — so any future async write path (a clipboard round trip, a docx import, a toolbar action gated on a fetch) inherits the original defect by omission. A design where the neutered method reports failure (as `pasteFormat` already does by returning `false`) would not depend on callers remembering. Flagged as approach fit, not as a bug in the two paths that do check.
searchedFor: grep editor.<mutator> call sites in packages/frontend/src

verdict.reason: Verified in-tree: `dispose()` (editor.ts:4434-4475) sets `disposed` and calls `neuterMutations(api)`, which only replaces named members in `MUTATING_METHODS` (editor.ts:1042-1072). The two live-handle accessors are plain closures with no disposal check — `getDoc: () => doc` and `getStore: () => (readOnly ? readStore : pageSetupGuardedStore)` (editor.ts:3317-3318) — and `readStore` is `readOnlyDocStore(docStore)` only when `readOnly` was baked in at construction (editor.ts:1123), which by definition is not the case for the editor built before an editor→viewer downgrade. The fallback `pageSetupGuardedStore` proxy forwards every other member bound to the real store and self-describes as "NOT an access-control boundary" (editor.ts:3251-3260, 3290-3310). No lower layer compensates: `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` only unsubscribes and clears `onRemoteChange` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:689-693), leaving writes live; `packages/docs/src/model` has no disposed/frozen guard. Meanwhile the `EditorAPI.isDisposed` contract asserts "A disposed editor is inert — every mutating method has been neutered" (editor.ts:407-414), and real callers do reach the document through these handles (docs-find-bar.tsx:66-67). So the asserted revocation boundary is wider than the implemented one; the same escape route #989 closed for `readOnly` has no disposal counterpart. Searched dispose(), the accessors, the store proxy, all `readOnlyDocStore`/`neuter` usages repo-wide, the frontend host effect (docs-view.tsx:549-590), the Yorkie store, the Doc model, and all `isDisposed` tests — found no counterexample.
